title: A judgment-call key needs a blind pick
statement: Where the key is a judgment call, such as the stronger of two answers, ship only when a judge that never saw the key picks it by a clear margin.
example: On a poem and a speech, all 4 blind picks matched the key, at 0.91 to 1.
detail: Two of the lesson engine's blocks have keys that are judgment calls: compare two answers, where the reader picks the stronger of two paragraphs, and direct the line, where the reader picks how a line should be spoken. In both, the judge gets the same material without the key and must pick the keyed option with a clear margin, so there is one defensible pick. On a poem and a speech all 4 such blocks were ready: the blind pick matched the delivery at 0.91 and 1 and the stronger paragraph at 0.99 and 0.99.
against: Judge precision is unmeasured: "bounded questions with the evidence supplied; their precision is not yet measured (v04)." (`g9/transformer/v01/QA.md`, line 46). In all 4 blocks the key sat in one position, B for the delivery and A for the stronger paragraph, so a judge's lean toward one position was not ruled out.
